Report: Auditor-General of Pakistan, Audit Report on the Accounts of Pakistan Railways, Audit Year 2024-25 (sources/AGP/agp_railways_2024_25.pdf)
Finding: Locomotives on miscellaneous services consumed 710,143 litres of HSD against a fixed quota of 316,664 litres across six formations in FY2023-24 - excess of 393,479 litres (Rs 109.26 million).
Note: INSTITUTIONALLY INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE METERING, from the body that audits the operator: quota breaches are resolved at the litre level per formation, which is only possible if fuel issue is metered - supporting the treatment of the published totals as measured. The excess is 0.3 percent of national railway diesel; a control problem, not a measurement one.

Finding: 2,000 HP line-haul locomotives used on shunting duties at Lahore loco shed from July 2022 to June 2024 despite lighter shunting locomotives (950-1,500 HP) being available - excess HSD loss Rs 110.16 million.
Note: Bears on the Tier 2 shunting assumption from an independent direction: shunting duty exists at material scale, is not separately published, and is sometimes performed by line-haul units - which blurs the very split the Tier 2 diagnostic declares as assumed.

Finding: 393,554 litres of HSD used above the fixed per-class trip rations (Rs 39.81 million), FY2020-21 formations audit.
Note: Trip rations exist PER LOCOMOTIVE CLASS and consumption is reconciled against them - further evidence of litre-level fuel accounting inside the operator.

Finding: 23,250 litres of HSD pilfered from the tanks of 12 locomotives stabled for repair (Rs 3.25 million), detected against the OP-27A record.
Note: The detection mechanism is the point: tank contents are recorded (OP-27A) and shortfalls surface in audit. Theft happens; unmetered fuel does not.

Finding: Extra fuel consumption due to speed restrictions, excess over fixed quota and non-operational functions amounting to Rs 1.77 billion.
Note: The operational-efficiency channel: track condition raises fuel per train-km. Consistent with the intensity series' FY2022 4.78 L/train-km against FY2024's 4.00.
